transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well... they say I’m here because I spent a lot of our savings on wood, lights, and display things for the house. I kept working on it even after dark. I just felt like if I stopped, the whole house—maybe the whole block—would miss its chance.
Can you tell me more about how you were feeling while you were working on the house? Were you feeling unusually excited, energetic, or like you didn’t need much sleep?

Yeah… I felt really charged up most days. Almost happy, like I was young again and had all this energy for it. But if my wife or one of the contractors questioned what I was doing, I’d get angry real quick. I’d start yelling before I even thought about it.
Have you ever had periods where your mood was extremely high or you felt unusually irritable for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least a few days in a row?

Yes. For several days at a time, most of the day, I’ve felt really charged up—almost joyful, like I’m young again. But I also get irritated fast. If my wife or the contractors question me, I get hot quick and start yelling.
Can you describe if there was a time when your mood was so high or so irritable that it was noticeably different from how you usually feel?

Yes… it was different. Most days I felt really charged up, almost joyful, like I was young again. But I’d also get irritated fast. If my wife or the contractors questioned me, I’d get hot and start yelling.

During those times when you felt so charged up and irritable, did you find yourself working on projects or moving around a lot more than usual, like you couldn’t slow down or stop yourself from doing things?

Yes. I couldn’t just sit in the chair like I normally might. I’d be up and moving around—out to the garden, then into the darkroom, then back to the porch. I’d be carrying tools around, fixing things before anybody even asked me to. It felt like I had to keep doing something.
During those times when you felt so charged up and irritable, did you find that you needed less sleep or could go with very little sleep without feeling tired?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember it being about sleep so much. I was up doing things, yeah, but I can’t say for sure that I needed less sleep or didn’t feel tired.
During those times when you felt so charged up, were you doing things constantly because you felt driven by an inner need to keep moving or working, even if it wasn’t necessary?

Yes, that’s how it felt. I couldn’t just sit in my chair like usual. I’d be up moving around—out to the garden, then into the darkroom, then back to the porch. I’d be carrying tools around, fixing things before anyone even asked me to. It just felt like I had to keep doing something.
During those times when you felt so charged up and restless, did you actually sleep less than usual — like sleeping only a few hours a night and still feeling fully energized?
I’m not sure about that part. I was up and moving around a lot, but I can’t really say I was only sleeping a few hours and feeling fully energized. I just don’t remember it that clearly.

Can you recall if there was a specific period when you felt this way for 7 days or more — almost like a switch flipped and you were consistently energized and restless, working on projects or moving around a lot without needing to slow down?

Yeah… it’s been longer than a week. I’d say it’s been going on about three months now, since the remodeling started and the whole house got turned upside down. Since then I’ve been like that—restless, doing things, not really slowing down much.

Can you describe if there was a specific time when your mood was consistently high or irritable along with this increased activity or restlessness, lasting for at least a full week without letting up?

Yes… for a good while now, most days I’ve felt really charged up, almost happy in a way, like I’m young again. But it doesn’t take much to set me off. If my wife or the contractors question what I’m doing, I get hot fast and start yelling. It’s been pretty steady like that, not just one day here and there.
Can you tell me if there was a time when your mood was clearly different from your usual self—like feeling unusually high, euphoric, or irritable—for a whole week or more without letting up?

Yeah, it’s been different from how I usually am. Most days I feel kind of charged up, almost joyful, like I’m young again. But then if my wife or the contractors question me, I get hot real fast and start yelling. It’s not just a little mood here and there.
Can you tell me if there was a time when your mood was clearly different from your usual self—like feeling unusually high, euphoric, or irritable—for a whole week or more without letting up?

Yeah, like I said, it’s been real different for me. Most days I feel charged up, almost joyful, like I’m young again. But then if my wife or the contractors question me, I get hot fast and start yelling. It’s not how I usually am.

Can you tell me if there was a specific time when your mood was clearly different from your usual self — like feeling unusually high, euphoric, or irritable — for a full week or more without letting up?

Yes. It’s been going on more than a week, pretty steady. Most days I feel charged up, almost joyful, like I’m young again. But if my wife or the contractors question me, I get hot real fast and start yelling. It’s not like my usual self.

During this time when you felt so energized and restless, did you notice that you actually needed less sleep — like sleeping only a couple of hours a night and still feeling completely awake and full of energy?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve been restless, but I haven’t been keeping track of how many hours I sleep. I can’t say for sure that I was sleeping only a couple hours and feeling fine.

During this time when you felt so energized and restless, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual — for example, sleeping only a couple of hours a night and still feeling completely awake and full of energy?

I don’t really know. I’ve been restless, yeah, but I can’t say I’ve only been sleeping a couple hours and feeling totally fine. I just haven’t been paying close enough attention to my sleep like that.

During this time when you felt so energized and restless, did you actually sleep much less than usual — like only sleeping a couple of hours a night and still feeling completely awake and full of energy?

I still can’t really say. I know I’ve been wound up and not resting right, but I haven’t noticed for sure that I’m only sleeping a couple hours and then feeling completely fine. I just don’t have a clear answer on that.
During this time when you felt so energized and restless, did you feel that you could go for a whole night with very little sleep and still feel completely awake and full of energy the next day?

I don’t know that I could say that. I’ve felt restless and keyed up, but I haven’t really noticed going a whole night on barely any sleep and then feeling completely full of energy the next day. I’m just not sure about that.

During this time when you felt so energized and restless, did you feel like you could get by on much less sleep than usual — like only sleeping a couple of hours and still feeling completely awake and full of energy the next day?

I’m not sure, doctor. I know I’ve been restless and kind of wound up, but I can’t honestly say I was sleeping just a couple hours and then felt wide awake the next day. I haven’t kept track of it that clearly.

During that time when you felt so energized and restless, did you feel like you needed a lot less sleep than usual — for example, sleeping only a few hours a night and still feeling completely energized the next day?
I really don’t know for sure. I’ve been restless, yeah, but I can’t say I only slept a few hours and then felt fully energized the next day. I just haven’t paid close enough attention to it.
